J.population: Direct eligible Lifelines Jansen source scenario: unrelated western-European adults, assumed age25-85, with reported unobserved exclusions and modeled fasting plasma glucose below7.
J.measurement: Integer age years; female1/women0/men; BMI kg/m^2; fresh fasting plasma glucose mmol/L; HbA1c NGSP percent representing documented IFCC scale under U_NGSP_SCALE.

B.population: Direct eligible Bao Shanghai source scenario: adults age20-80 inclusive under assumed upper support, prior diagnosed diabetes and reported exclusions assumed absent; screen-detected diabetes allowed.
B.measurement: Integer age years; female1/women0/men; BMI kg/m^2; 10-hour fasting venous plasma glucose mmol/L by glucose oxidase; HPLC HbA1c percent, printed instrument HLC-73G7 retained.

M.population: Direct eligible MIND rural Yanlou/Shandong follow-up source scenario: age61-80 inclusive, reported dementia/disability exclusions assumed, known diabetes included.
M.measurement: Integer age years; female1/women0/men; prior-year BMI kg/m^2; 2019 overnight fasting serum glucose mmol/L by glucose oxidase CS-600B, not the separate plasma measure; whole-blood HPLC HbA1c percent.

T.population: CHNS 2009 released-data analytical population: adults aged 35-74 years inclusive, linked person/wave records with documented male/female category and available age, BMI from released height/weight, central-serum glucose and whole-blood HbA1c under the frozen common-complete-case release policy. No diabetes, treatment or pregnancy exclusion is claimed. Age/sex composition is not supplied. This is a selected analytical sample, not a nationally representative population; no participant input.
T.measurement: Target integer age years35-74; female1/women0/men; released-height/weight BMI kg/m^2; central-serum glucose mmol/L; whole-blood HbA1c percent; complete-case selected analytical population.

assumptions.description: Each context is a directly specified joint law for its eligible analytical population. No parent population, exclusion frequency or actual participant reconstruction is claimed. Absent exclusion variables remain conditioning assumptions.

Age and female are mutually independent and independent of three mutually independent latent biometric factors. A lower-triangular correlation construction links BMI, glucose and HbA1c. Unreported age/sex relations are not identified by evidence; independence is a simplifying scenario, not a measured null.

The latent BMI-glucose correlation is 0.25 in every context, an unsupported structural assumption. Jansen HbA1c associations determine two covariance entries, not two coefficients pasted into a joint conditional equation.

The Jansen standardized BMI-HbA1c association is used as the latent BMI-HbA1c correlation in B/M/T. This scale and population transfer is unsupported. Jansen age/sex independence makes its separate adjusted slopes equal the corresponding bivariate projections only within this scenario.

J uses independent centered uniform latent factors to specify an eligible bounded affine biometric law. The resulting biomarker bounds are induced mathematical model support, not asserted physiological limits or a clipped/conditioned Gaussian. The glucose support is wholly below 7 mmol/L.

B/M/T use lognormal BMI and glucose and shifted-lognormal HbA1c with shift 2.152. This imposes a scale-compatible lower HbA1c support without asserting a physiological threshold. Lognormal tails and Gaussian latent dependence are assumptions, with unbounded upper support and finite polynomial moments.

Source integer ages are assigned finite categorical probabilities proportional to discretized Gaussian bin masses using published age locations and dispersions; J support25..85 and B support20..80 are model assumptions, M support61..80 is eligibility. Bao dispersion from IQR uses an assumed normal precursor. These direct integer laws do not claim exact reproduction of continuous-age summaries. Target age is discrete uniform35..74; no target composition is known.

female=1 denotes women and 0 denotes men. Source probabilities use source count fractions, with J male fraction complemented. This is not known source numeric coding or a weighted population proportion. Target female probability0.5 is assumed. Native gender_binary is a temporary alias of this two-category partition.

J and M mean/individual-SD summaries initialize appropriate final margins. Bao log dispersion is inferred from the two quartile endpoints under a lognormal assumption, with the reported median retained; asymmetric quartiles need not match. Individual SDs are not SEs and source sample counts do not create precision weights.

Qualified source calculations use complete generated values, equal weights, intercept-including separate Jansen OLS models, and average ties for MIND Spearman. Original weights, analytic row selection, processing and MIND filling/tie details remain unknown. Strict comparisons remain unavailable.

Generated glucose denotes J/B fasting plasma, M fasting serum and T central serum in mmol/L. Native aliases preserve these context-specific meanings. BMI/HbA1c assays, fasting protocols and sampling timing are not asserted equivalent; no plasma/serum conversion is performed.
The documented NGSP=0.09148*IFCC+2.152 relation supplies J levels and SD conversion and its temporary reverse IFCC view. It is a representation relation, not assay equivalence or a glucose model.

J modeled eligible population assumes the reported diabetes/anemia/missing-variable exclusions and unrelated western-European sampling without observing those variables. Adult support25..85 is assumed; only the generated FPG cutoff is enforced by the law.

B age20 is included, adopting the explicit under20 exclusion over ambiguous prose. Prior diabetes, cancer, severe psychiatric disturbance, chronic kidney disease, pregnancy, glucocorticoid treatment and questionnaire exclusions are assumed, not verified. Screen-detected diabetes is not excluded; there is no glucose upper cutoff.

M age61..80 is represented directly. Freedom from dementia/functional disability, rural follow-up selection and the prior-year BMI/2019 lab timing are assumed. Known diabetes is allowed. Unknown mean/mode filling is not reconstructed.

Target BMI/glucose/HbA1c margins are provisionally transported from Bao; serum glucose-HbA1c latent dependence is transported from MIND; the BMI link comes from Jansen. This deliberate dependency path is not an identified target joint law. Target age/sex are independent assumed compositions and target complete-case selection does not imply diabetes/treatment/pregnancy exclusions.

All scientific constants are frozen decimal floating values. Analytic source-correlation identities use ideal mathematics; finite-decimal approximation and finite random draws need not hit published points. On overflow, underflow, nonfinite output, support failure or rank failure the whole execution raises; there is no clipping, retry, seed replacement, resampling or row deletion.

Residual variation is simulated individual variation. No evidence uncertainty distribution, confidence score, precision weighting, causal claim or calibrated target inference is supplied. All source summaries from a cohort are dependent descriptions, not independent confirmations.

active_context.derivation: T is the required target selector; context switching changes no other scientific bytes.

contexts.derivation: J affine means/SDs use Table1 and NGSP conversion; J two covariance entries use each separate Table2 slope times predictorSD/IFCC-SD. B Gaussian-copula log margins use medians and log-IQR/(2*Phi^-1(.75)); its latent glucose-HbA1c r is log(1+Pearson*sqrt(expm1(sg^2)*expm1(sh^2)))/(sg*sh). M log margins use mean/SD and latent r=2*sin(pi*Spearman/6). Source ages use integer bin weights normalized over declared supports. T copies B biometric margins, M latent glucose-HbA1c dependence, common J latent BMI link; age uniform and female.5 are assumptions, never target estimates.

shared.derivation: r_bh=.13*4.1/3 is a standardized J covariance ratio used as a latent association elsewhere only by assumption; r_bg=.25 is assumed. Uniform bound sqrt3 gives unit variance in ideal algebra. Independent standardized factors and Gaussian copula are distributional choices.
